chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson studies faith strengthened through Christ's saving work. Why does the account of Christ's place support the hearers' received hope?
chapters.1.summary: Paul and Timothy write to the saints at Colossae. They thank God for the faith of readers whom Epaphras taught. They pray that the readers be filled with knowledge of God’s will. The Father moved them from darkness into the kingdom of his Son. A passage of praise follows. The Son is God’s image, and all things were created through him. He is head of the body, and through him God reconciles all things. Paul rejoices in his sufferings and labors to present everyone mature in Christ.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches remaining rooted in Christ against deceptive influences. How does holding the head differ from depending on added rules?
chapters.2.summary: Paul says he struggles for the readers and for those at Laodicea. All the treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ. They should walk in him as they were taught. He warns against philosophy and empty deceit built on human tradition. In Christ all the fullness of deity lives in bodily form. God forgave them and nailed the record of debt to the cross. No one should judge them about food, festivals, new moons, or Sabbaths. Rules like “Don’t handle, nor taste, nor touch” have no value against the flesh.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches putting away former conduct and practicing shared care. How does seeking what is above change conduct toward earthly neighbors?
chapters.3.summary: Paul says the readers were raised with Christ and should seek the things above. Their life is hidden with Christ in God. They are to put to death immorality, greed, anger, and lying. In the new man there is no Greek or Jew, slave or free. They are to put on compassion, kindness, and patience, and to forgive. Love binds all together, and Christ’s peace should rule. Instructions follow for wives, husbands, children, fathers, and servants. Whatever they do, they are to do it as for the Lord.
chapters.4.lds: Why do personal messengers matter beside the request to exchange letters?
chapters.4.summary: Masters are told to give their servants what is just and equal. Paul asks for prayer that a door will open for the word. He is in chains for it. He sends Tychicus and Onesimus to report his news. Aristarchus, Mark, Jesus called Justus, Epaphras, Luke, and Demas send greetings. He greets the brothers in Laodicea and the assembly in the house of Nymphas. The letter is to be read in Laodicea too. Paul signs with his own hand and asks them to remember his chains.
